# Checkbox

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

forms · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a yes or no the form sends later, or one item of a list someone can pick several of. For a
setting that takes effect at once, a Switch reads better. It is one element: Base UI's checkbox,
as a native button.

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from 'topclassui/checkbox'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="terms">I accept the terms</label>
<Checkbox id="terms" name="terms" defaultChecked />
```

**A name is required.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`), `aria-label` or
`aria-labelledby`; the type refuses a Checkbox with none. The root is a `<button>` with
`role="checkbox"`, so the label names it in the server HTML and a click on the label presses it.
A label that wraps the box names it too; the type still asks for one of the three, so give it an `id`:

```tsx
<label>
  <Checkbox id="news" name="news" />
  Send me product news
</label>
```

Checkbox draws no label of its own: you write it, and later a Field will.

**The state is `checked`, `defaultChecked` and `onCheckedChange`**, Base UI's names. `value`
keeps its native meaning: the string the form receives when the box is ticked (`on` by default).
Pass `checked` to control it. Your handler runs first, with Base UI's details, so
`details.cancel()` leaves the box as it was.

**`indeterminate`** draws a dash and sets `aria-checked="mixed"`, for a box whose list is partly
picked. It is yours to clear: a press calls `onCheckedChange(true)`, and the box stays mixed until
you drop `indeterminate`. A mixed box sends nothing, not even its `uncheckedValue`, before the page
hydrates and after; it sends its value once you drop `indeterminate`.

```tsx
export function SelectAll({ all, some, onAll }: { all: boolean, some: boolean, onAll: (next: boolean) => void }) {
  return <Checkbox aria-label="Select all" checked={all} indeterminate={some && !all} onCheckedChange={onAll} />
}
```

**The keyboard.** Space toggles it. Enter does not: inside a form it submits the form, as a
native checkbox does.

**The form.** With a `name`, Base UI serves a hidden checkbox beside the button: unticked sends
nothing, ticked sends `name=on`, and `uncheckedValue` makes an unticked box send that string.
`form` ties it to a form it is not inside. Before the page hydrates the form sends the default.
**A form reset**, a reset button or a React 19 form action that settles brings the box back to
its `defaultChecked` of the latest render, on screen and in the form; a controlled box keeps its
owner's value. A reset calls no `onCheckedChange`.

**`required` means "must be ticked"**, as on a native checkbox. Before the page hydrates, the
browser sends the focus of a blocked submit to the hidden input, a box of 1 px.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid`: the line of the box turns red and thickens, ticked or not.
**`disabled`** is the real attribute, so the box leaves the tab order and the form sends nothing.
**`readOnly`** keeps it in the form and says so to a screen reader; it has no look of its own.

**The target is 24 px, 44 px under a finger**, whatever `size` draws: the focus ring is around
the box. `size="custom"` draws no box size: give the box one from your own CSS.

**The radius is `rounded-chip`**: 4 px, and 8 px in Ocean, where the `xs` and `sm` boxes are
circles, ticked or not: only the tick or the dash tells them from a radio.

**`parent`** reaches Base UI, but does nothing without a `CheckboxGroup`, which is not built.

**A wrapper** takes `CheckboxProps`. `Omit<CheckboxProps, 'x'>` merges the three ways to name a
box into one where none is required.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Root`, `Indicator`, `role="checkbox"`, `aria-checked` with `mixed`, Space | as they are |
| Enter, which submits the form the box is in | as it is |
| `checked`, `defaultChecked`, `onCheckedChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names; the value is held for the form reset |
| `indeterminate`, `name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `parent`, `inputRef` | passed through |
| a `<span>` root | always a native `<button>`: `nativeButton` and `render` are not props |

### Not built

`CheckboxGroup` and the parent box that goes with it (their own catalog row), `tone` (one is
drawn), a label child, a hint and a required mark (a Field's), a hover look, a read-only look,
the invalid ring that is always on, a skeleton (use `Skeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { Checkbox } from 'topclassui/checkbox'
```

## Props

Required: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` or `id`. Every other prop below is optional.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | **yes**, or `aria-labelledby` or `id` | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `id` | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `id` | **yes**, or `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | Merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with the checkbox's own. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid, and the line of the box turns to danger and thickens. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLButtonElement>` | - | The root element, which is a `<button>`. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The toggle scale of the drawn box and its mark; custom emits no size classes. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
